A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, Table 1, and Appendices A–D. Sections and results can be matched despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original batch classification and online Criteo experiments, including log-loss and AUC results.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the work's original experiments and their results in Figures 1–6.

M1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds an unequal-bag variant alongside the retained three-subset algorithm: it divides 2m bags into two subsets, reserving the m smallest for loss estimation and using the others for moment and label-marginal estimation. The centered loss estimator and tournament remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate MNIST even-versus-odd, CIFAR-10 animal-versus-machine and cat-versus-rest, Higgs, Adult, and online Criteo click prediction. The unequal-bag extension is theoretical, without added experimental coverage.

E2.justification: GENERALUPM is compared with the same EasyLLP and proportion-matching baselines in every corresponding experiment. Citation-format changes do not alter comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D retain the data preparation, architectures, label smoothing, bag sizes, 4096-example batches, learning-rate grid, and online 2^16-example chunks. The new theoretical sample split does not change the reported experimental protocol.

E4.justification: The bag-size comparisons, online trajectories, complete log-loss plots, and supplementary AUC analyses are retained. No new ablation, robustness experiment, or case study is added.

E5.justification: Both report ten repetitions for batch experiments, five for online experiments, randomized shuffling and initialization, and error bars representing one standard error. No uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Figures 1–6 retain identical underlying plots, including all appendix results. The reported performance rankings and findings are unchanged; panel rearrangement and revised interpretation introduce no new empirical results.

T1.justification: V1 only remarks that the analysis extends to unequal bag sizes. V2 adds Appendix B.3, Theorem B.2, and a proof sketch deriving the sample-complexity guarantee using average bag size and the new split construction. This supplies substantive formal treatment of the previously informal extension; the existing main theorems remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about low-variance debiasing, general losses, binary and multiclass guarantees, and large-bag empirical advantages are retained. Unequal-bag robustness is newly emphasized in the conclusion but was already claimed in v1's Section 3.

C2.justification: Section 4 expands the explanation of PM's small-bag performance through proper losses and realizability, and attributes its deterioration at larger bag sizes to increasing bias. V1 mainly used the realizable optimum to explain MNIST. The substantive limitations in Section 5 remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D.3 corrects expectation estimation from the remaining B−1 'batches' to the remaining B−1 'bags' within a training batch. This clarifies implementation without establishing a changed experiment. Architectures, hyperparameters, and computing-resource disclosures are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Franco et al. (2023) to position its bag-dependence assumptions and Høgsgaard and Paudice (2025) when discussing infinite hypothesis classes. It removes the Google Privacy Sandbox citation. The principal comparisons with earlier LLP research remain.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the abstract, makes local prose and terminology edits, expands selected explanations, adds an Impact Statement, and switches to author–year citations. The main section sequence and appendix organization are largely preserved, with the unequal-bag subsection inserted.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one column to two, with extensive equation and float reflow. Figure 1 changes from a three-plus-two to a two-plus-three panel arrangement; figures, Algorithm 1, and Table 1 are resized or relocated. Appendix plots are redistributed and enlarged, without new plotted content.

improvement.justification: The explicit unequal-bag construction and Theorem B.2's proof sketch make an earlier informal claim more assessable, while the Appendix D.3 correction removes an implementation ambiguity. These are limited gains because the central guarantees and empirical evidence remain unchanged. The added proof still contains a stray S3 reference despite defining only S1 and S2.
